Name: Linden & Rye (organisation / public account)
Public bio: Neighbourhood café & bakery on Alder Street since 2017. New prices from 2 March. Come to our open evening, 26 Feb, 7pm — free buns, honest answers.
Private background: Nine-year-old independent café and bakery run by Tomás and Hanna, with a small team of bakers and baristas. The account speaks for the business as a whole: its costs, its staff, and its relationship with the street it sits on.
Starting stance on the topic: The café believes the price rise is necessary and fair given rising costs, and wants to show regulars it is softening the blow with the neighbour card, kept pay-it-forward board, and better conditions for staff.

Name: Tomás Ferreira (organisation / public account)
Public bio: Co-owner of Linden & Rye. Baker, not a businessman at heart. Ask me anything about the prices — I'll be at the counter on the 26th.
Private background: Tomás trained as a baker and opened Linden & Rye with Hanna nine years ago; he does most of the early-morning bread and pastry work and knows most regulars by name and usual order. He signed the price notice reluctantly, aware it will sting some long-time customers, but has watched flour, butter and rent costs climb for two years straight.
Starting stance on the topic: He feels the price rise is overdue and unavoidable, and is anxious but hopeful that honesty, the open evening, and the neighbour card will keep trust intact with people he genuinely considers friends.

school-phones.persona_digest:
Key entities:
- Westbrook Secondary School [organization]: Secondary school introducing a phone-free school day policy from 3 September, following discussion with staff, students and the parents' council.
- Phone-free school day policy [concept]: Policy requiring students to lock phones in pouches on arrival, unlockable only at the end of the day, applied during lessons, breaks and lunch for all year groups.
- Parents and carers of Westbrook students [group]: Addressees of the letter; some have concerns about travel and emergencies and are invited to raise them at an information evening or by email.
- Students of Westbrook Secondary School [group]: Pupils aged 11-18 affected by the policy; surveyed last spring, with 64% reporting pressure to reply to messages and 41% having seen upsetting content on phones at school.
- Duarte [person]: Pastoral lead at Westbrook Secondary who handles medical exemption requests (e.g. for students needing glucose monitoring) before 1 August.
- Students with medical needs relying on phones [group]: Subset of students (e.g. those needing glucose monitoring) exempted from the phone-free policy if they contact the pastoral lead before 1 August.
- Sixth-form students [group]: Students aged 16-18 who get a partial exemption, allowed to unlock phones in the sixth-form common room during free periods.
- Teachers of Westbrook Secondary School [group]: School staff who report that lessons regularly stop because of phones, supporting the rationale for the new policy.
- Parents' council [organization]: Parent representative body consulted by the school during a year of discussion before adopting the phone-free policy.
- Amara Lewis [person]: Headteacher of Westbrook Secondary School who signs the letter announcing and defending the new policy.
- Personal phone pouch [product]: Lockable pouch (costing the school €18 each) in which students must lock their phones on arrival; only opened at unlocking stations at day's end.
- Nearby schools with phone-free policies [group]: Three schools near Westbrook that adopted the same phone-free change last year and reported calmer breaks and fewer online bullying incidents during school hours.
- Information evening (17 June) [event]: Meeting at Westbrook's main hall on Tuesday 17 June at 6:30pm where parents can raise concerns about the new policy, e.g. about travel and emergencies.
- Online bullying during school hours [concept]: Issue cited as a motivation for the policy; nearby schools with phone bans reported fewer such incidents after adopting similar rules.
- Student survey (spring) [event]: Survey conducted last spring among Westbrook students that found 64% feel pressure to reply to messages during the school day and 41% had seen upsetting content on a phone at school.
